sentences.text: The premise holds on this record: every one of the four quarters clears 70%, and the tightest quarter, Q3 FY2026, still has room of 1.69x a typical quarterly move.

That room is real but not deep. One typical move would not break the test, and in 69% of resampled paths it held for four more quarters, which also means roughly a third of paths built from the margin's own past swings did not.
The streak is also recent rather than habitual: the test held in only 6 of 20 past filing-date readings, and the four-quarter run now in place matches its longest run.

The quarter just before this window shows what breaks it. Q1 FY2026 fell to 60.5% because of the H20 inventory and purchase-obligation charge, which the filing names as a prior-year item, not an operating trend.

For a buy decision, the claim matters mainly because the price leans on margin. The reverse DCF assumes a 65.2% operating margin every year, and at the industry's 90th-percentile margin the same price would need 28.1% annual growth instead of 13.4%.

So the claim supports a precondition of the valuation at the 2026-09-30 price, but on its own it is not a reason to buy. It says nothing about whether margins persist, and nothing about the period after the CEO's resignation, which comes later than the newest quarter in the record.
The margin is rising, not merely holding: it is up on a year earlier, and the filing attributes the gain to Blackwell Ultra mix.
Against its industry the level is exceptional, ranking 4 of 63 against a class median of 41.2%, though SIC 3674 is a broad peer set.
The implications check out: fiscal 2026 margin cleared 70%, and the latest operating margin clears 50%, so the strength is not limited to the gross line.

Inventory is outrunning the business. Inventory days rose to 119.3 from 105.6, and inventory grew faster than revenue, which is the opposite of what the claim implies; that is the same kind of exposure that produced the H20 charge.
The margin is no higher than two years ago, so the recent rise is a recovery from the charge-hit low rather than new ground.
The filing already notes a net unfavorable effect on gross margin in the latest quarter, so the 75.0% level absorbs headwinds that the record does not size beyond that.
Whether the inventory build, now at 119.3 days, sells through without another excess-inventory charge like the one that cut margin to 60.5%.
Whether margins stay near the 65.2% operating margin that the 2026-09-30 price assumes; the gross-margin streak is necessary for that but not sufficient.
How margins behave in the first quarter reported under interim leadership, which no filing in the record covers yet.

conditions.text: A quarterly gross margin below 70% in a later 10-Q would break the four-quarter test.
A quarterly operating margin below 50% would fail a corollary the claim implies, and would undercut the margin the price assumes.
An 8-K disclosing an inventory or purchase-obligation charge would signal a repeat of the H20 episode that broke the 70% line before.
